::: {.callout-warning}
## Try it on a disposable project
Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds
(`proj build`) can modify or remove files. Recovery covers only recorded managed paths.
**Never run production builds on the only copy of important work.**
Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.
:::

::: {.hero}
projcli runs the analysis steps you choose from a small project configuration.
Start with the preview example below; production build safety is still being improved.

[Get started](tutorial.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Check installation options](install.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

without compiling Rust. It delivers the M1 local CLI preview; M2 and later

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
## Choose your steps

List the scripts that belong to your analysis. Start with one Python script;
add R or rendered reports when your project needs them.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
## Keep paths consistent

Select a project explicitly with `--project`. Child commands keep that project
context, even when an analysis changes its working folder.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
## Preview as you work

`proj build-dev` runs analysis without the CLI publishing outputs or changing
the project version. Your scripts still control the files they write.
:::
:::

## A small first project

Put the analysis steps in `_proj.yml`:

```yaml
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
```

These paths are explicit, not runtime defaults. The Python example uses
`cache`; `raw-data` and `output` match the local setup preset.
The [tutorial](tutorial.qmd) explains their roles and local-only initialization.

Run the preview from your project folder:

```bash
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
```

The [step-by-step example](tutorial.qmd) supplies the script, a tiny dataset,
and the result to check. It uses Python's standard library.
